A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OXtal study. All 38 pages, including Appendices A–I, figures, tables, and equations, are available and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original crystal-prediction experiments, baseline evaluations, ablations, conformer robustness tests, and chemical analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark evaluations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, loss components, and detailed training and inference procedures are retained. Section 3.1 now mentions the sampling probability and restricts frontier subsampling to cases where no full shell fits, but both details already appear in v1 Appendix B.2.1 and Algorithm 1. Equation 7 receives a formal correction rather than an explicitly introduced method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 594,202-crystal training collection, rigid and flexible test sets, CSP blind tests 5–7, and supplementary chemical, conformer, and larger-crystal scenarios. No represented task or dataset coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: A-Transformer and AssembleFlow remain in the main comparisons, AlphaFold3 remains in the rigid-set appendix comparison, and the same physics-based submissions form the DFT comparisons. Revised baseline scores do not introduce different comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 changes the stated COMPACK settings from a distance and angle threshold of 50% to a distance threshold of 50% and an angle threshold of 75 degrees. This revises a previously stated evaluation setting; the PDFs do not establish whether evaluations were rerun. Other splits, budgets, sample counts, and metric thresholds are retained.

E4.justification: The cropping, shell-radius, model-size, conformer robustness, larger-block, additional-sampling, and chemical analyses are retained. Table 6 revises reference baseline scores, but the ablation conditions, OXtal ablation results, and analytical questions remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Seed and run reporting is unchanged, including training seed 42, inference seeds 0–29, and AssembleFlow's three-seed, 63-run procedure. There are no additions or revisions to uncertainty estimation, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Corrections are confined to existing baseline entries in Tables 1, 2, 3, and 6. AssembleFlow's rigid RecS/RecC changes from 0.001/0.020 to 0.211/0.760; its flexible ColS/RecS/RecC changes from 0.671/0.035/0.100 to 0.883/0.021/0.140. Table 2 changes A-Transformer's collision rates from zero to 0.833/0.967/0.950 for CSP5/6/7 and AssembleFlow's CSP7 RecC from 0.286 to 0.250, matching values already in v1 Table 6. Some baseline rankings change substantially, but OXtal and DFT entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 7 changes the corruption distribution's conditioning from aligned x0 to x0, retaining alignment inside the losses and removing the dependence on a prediction-aligned target from that distribution. Section 2.1 also corrects the permutation expression to use fractional coordinates u rather than x. Proposition 1 and its Appendix A proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same claims about an all-atom diffusion model, lattice-free S4 training, strong packing prediction, and lower inference cost than physics-based approaches. The numerical corrections do not lead to revised core claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning kinetic and thermodynamic regularities, polymorph diversity, conformer robustness, and long-range generalization are retained. The limitations concerning ranking, relaxation, crystallization context, planar-packing preference, and the scope of the energy analysis are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit model-code availability statement and repository link. The PDFs support this added access information, without establishing the repository's contents or accessibility. Existing hardware, preprocessing, architecture, and training details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The collision-metric citation changes from Cordero et al. (2008), 'Covalent radii revisited,' to Guha et al. (2006), 'The blue obelisk—interoperability in chemical informatics,' with the corresponding bibliography replacement. Related-work discussions and broader novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized spelling, grammar, duplication, and cross-reference edits, clarifies the main-text sampling description, adds an author affiliation, and replaces the preprint header with the ICLR 2026 publication header. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All 20 figures and 13 tables are retained with the same underlying displays. Changes include limited caption edits, corrected boldface in Table 6, publication headers, and modest text and table reflow. There is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting consistency: Section 3.1 better matches the existing sampling algorithm, Equation 7 corrects the corruption distribution, and Table 2 resolves baseline discrepancies with Appendix D. The explicit COMPACK angle setting and added code link also help reproducibility. These are useful, limited improvements; the PDFs do not establish whether revised settings or scores reflect reruns, and the underlying experimental coverage and main conclusions remain stable.
